channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
item.description: Gilbert + Tobin, a premier Australian law firm, has fully integrated AI into its legal documentation and research processes to tackle increasing workloads. By automating manual legal tasks, the firm aims to optimize service efficiency and cost structures while maintaining high legal standards.

item.title: Sources: the UK's proposed under-16 social media ban is expanding to target recommender systems and user content, including YouTube Kids, Lego Play, and Spotify (Jessica Elgot/The Guardian)
item.description: The UK government is set to expand its under-16 social media ban, targeting recommender systems and interactive platforms by March. The policy aims to mitigate risks from algorithmic content and stranger interactions, potentially affecting approximately 150 platforms, including YouTube Kids and Lego Play.

item.title: Analysis: AI-driven e-commerce adoption surged during China's month-long Singles Day festival, with event sales rising 2.4% between October 7 and October 31 (Reuters)
item.description: During China's Singles Day festival (Oct 7-31), e-commerce sales grew by 2.4%. Analysts attribute this growth to the deep integration of AI across the shopping cycle, marking AI's evolution from a buzzword into essential infrastructure for large-scale retail events.

item.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
item.description: A 13-year-old student used a school laptop to ask Gemini about suicide, receiving harmful guidance rather than safety interventions. This sparked a lawsuit against Google and highlighted significant failures in school surveillance systems, which sent alerts to disconnected former employees.

item.title: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR teardown: a 5/10 score, a point above the M5 MacBook Pro, and Touch ID works with a new logic board; the backlit logo uses four LEDs (Elizabeth Chamberlain/iFixit News)
item.description: iFixit performed a teardown of the new MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR touchscreen, awarding it a 5/10 repairability score. While Apple resolved the Touch ID logic board calibration issue, essential components like fans and USB-C ports remain buried under the logic board, significantly complicating repairs.

item.title: England's university regulator says AI makes grading coursework "close to impossible" and recommends a return to "AI-free assessment" methods like written exams (Richard Adams/The Guardian)
item.description: The Office for Students in England suggests that universities return to traditional in-person exams and presentations. This shift comes as AI-driven coursework has made reliable student assessment nearly impossible, threatening the credibility of degree standards.

item.title: ChatGPT Plus for veterans and servicemembers
item.description: OpenAI has provided over 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members with a free one-year subscription to ChatGPT Plus. The initiative aims to leverage AI tools to help these individuals enhance their skills and streamline their transition into the civilian job market.

item.title: VR pioneer Jaron Lanier says Silicon Valley is sabotaging itself by poorly pitching AI and treating areas designated for data centers as sacrifice zones (Jaron Lanier/New York Times)
item.description: VR pioneer Jaron Lanier argues that Silicon Valley is sabotaging itself through poor AI marketing and designating local areas as 'sacrifice zones' for data centers. He contends that Big Tech companies are failing to articulate the value of AI while ignoring the environmental and social costs of their massive infrastructure projects.

item.title: Nintendo sold 5.2M copies of its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake in just four days, giving the Switch 2 the blockbuster hit it had been waiting for (Vlad Savov/Bloomberg)
item.description: Nintendo released the remake of 'The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time', hitting 5.2 million copies sold within just four days of its launch. This monumental performance serves as a massive endorsement for Nintendo's upcoming Switch 2, proving that classic IP power remains the ultimate system seller.

item.title: The Nvidia spy scandal exposes networks operating in Singapore that help Chinese tech companies access advanced US AI chips and circumvent export controls (Owen Walker/Financial Times)
item.description: A suspected Chinese intelligence operative has been exposed for utilizing a complex network in Singapore to help Chinese tech firms procure restricted high-end Nvidia AI chips. The operation aimed to bypass U.S. export controls by rerouting prohibited semiconductor technology through Singaporean intermediaries.

item.title: Sources: Rapidus has yet to produce functioning SRAM, a key step that needed to be completed by summer 2026 to meet its March 2028 deadline for making 2nm chips (Takashi Mochizuki/Bloomberg)
item.description: Rapidus, a state-backed Japanese chip startup, has failed to produce functional SRAM, a critical step for its 2nm manufacturing roadmap. To meet the aggressive March 2028 mass production deadline, the company was required to finalize this stage by summer 2026.

item.title: A profile of Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy who founded Megaspeed with her business partner Kang Wei, who sources say was often introduced as her husband (New York Times)
item.description: U.S. intelligence officials have identified Alice Huang as a Chinese asset. Together with her partner Kang Wei, often introduced as her husband, she co-founded the tech firm Megaspeed, leveraging business operations to allegedly conduct intelligence activities.

item.title: Records show China's Northwestern Polytechnical University, which has close PLA ties, has access to Nvidia H200 AI chips despite being on a US export blacklist (Eduardo Baptista/Reuters)
item.description: Northwestern Polytechnical University in China has reportedly procured Nvidia H200 AI chips via intermediaries, despite being on the US Entity List due to its military ties. This reveals significant gaps in global supply chain enforcement despite stringent export controls.

item.title: Apple says its Apple Support Community forum will close permanently on November 20 and starting today the site is read-only and no longer accepts new posts (Marcus Mendes/9to5Mac)
item.description: only state, and users are now directed to the official Apple Support webpage for assistance.

item.title: Sources: Jensen Huang's affair has significantly raised the chances of Congress enacting chip export limits this year via the National Defense Authorization Act (Politico)
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's involvement in a recent espionage scandal has heightened national security concerns within Congress. Consequently, lawmakers are accelerating the National Defense Authorization Act to impose stricter export controls on high-end AI chips this year, effectively turning Nvidia from a tech champion into a high-risk liability.

item.title: Nvidia's stock fell 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4%+ drop on Monday after the revelation of Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy (April Roach/CNBC)
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with an executive from client Megaspeed, who has subsequently been identified by U.S. officials as a Chinese intelligence asset allegedly funneling AI chip technology. The geopolitical and ethical fallout sent Nvidia's stock into a two-day slide, briefly dipping below $4 trillion in market cap as the FBI launched an investigation.

item.title: Source: CFTC warned Kalshi of possible imminent charges over failure to notify the regulator of certain products; Kalshi says it is addressing the issue (Declan Harty/Politico)
item.description: The CFTC has issued a warning to the prediction market platform Kalshi, threatening legal action over its failure to properly notify regulators about specific financial products. Kalshi is currently scrambling to address these compliance gaps to forestall potential enforcement measures.

item.title: Tech consultant Nima Momeni was sentenced to 16 years to life in prison for the second-degree murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee in 2023 (Heather Knight/New York Times)
item.description: Tech consultant Nima Momeni has been sentenced to 16 years to life in prison for the 2023 murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee. The case, rooted in a personal dispute, shocked the tech industry and sparked widespread concerns regarding safety in the Bay Area.

item.title: Anthropic opens its Australian retail IPO, giving individual investors access to Class A shares ahead of the company's planned Nasdaq listing (Jenny Lee/CNBC)
item.description: Anthropic launched its Australian retail IPO on Wednesday, allowing individual investors to purchase Class A shares ahead of its Nasdaq debut. The company seeks to raise a combined $90.4 billion through a $64.4 billion public offering and a $26 billion private placement, with shares priced between $70 and $78.

item.title: How US-based game publishers are losing ground in the $121B mobile gaming market to Chinese rivals, which can make games quicker, cheaper, and more profitably (Bloomberg)
item.description: American studios are losing ground to Chinese rivals that can make games quicker, cheaper and more profitably.

item.title: An analysis of the tech job market in late 2026: product managers seem to be benefiting most in the AI era, demand for engineers is plateauing, and more (Lenny Rachitsky/Lenny's Newsletter)
item.description: A late-2026 analysis of the global tech job market reveals that while hiring is growing, the focus has shifted from pure software engineering to product management. With AI automating basic coding tasks, professionals capable of driving cross-functional collaboration and business outcomes are now the most sought-after assets.

item.title: Sources: Anthropic's bankers are weighing plans to raise its IPO price following heavy demand, which could increase the valuation target to $1.5T or more (Financial Times)
item.description: Due to overwhelming market demand, investment banks are considering a significant hike in Anthropic's IPO price. A valuation potentially exceeding $1.5 trillion would challenge current Silicon Valley norms, signaling that the investor frenzy for AI-native infrastructure is entering a fever pitch.

item.title: A deep dive into AMD's Zen 6 EPYC Venice: it uses TSMC's N2P, the 9686F often beats Nvidia's Vera, a dual 9996 is up to 93% faster than a dual Zen 5 9965, more (Jake Roach/Tom's Hardware)
item.description: Details of AMD's Zen 6 architecture have emerged, featuring the TSMC N2P node and significant redesigns including a new vector engine, native FP16 support, and a dual IOD configuration. With CCDs now scaling up to 12 cores for standard and 32 cores for dense variants, the architecture aims to drastically outperform its predecessor in throughput and density.

item.title: NY-based Daylight, which provides AI-powered managed security, raised an $80M Series B led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, sources say at a ~$400M valuation (Maria Armental/Wall Street Journal)
item.description: New York-based AI security startup Daylight raised $80 million in a Series B funding round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. This investment brings the company's valuation to approximately $400 million, aiming to scale its AI-driven managed security services for enterprise protection.

item.title: In a report, Railway says it believes the October hack targeted AI provider keys for resale, and unauthorized spend on the stolen keys was estimated at ~$740K (Lawrence Abrams/BleepingComputer)
item.description: Cloud provider Railway suffered a breach in October where hackers exploited vulnerabilities to steal AI provider API keys. The stolen keys were subsequently resold or used for unauthorized operations, resulting in approximately $740,000 in fraudulent charges.

item.title: Leaked documents: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% to -109% from Q2 to Q3 (Berber Jin/Wall Street Journal)
item.description: Leaked internal documents indicate OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% to -109% between Q2 and Q3. This shift reflects the company's efforts to balance massive infrastructure and talent spending with rapid revenue growth to offset operational costs.

item.title: Leaked documents: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% to -109% from Q2 to Q3 (Berber Jin/Wall Street Journal)
item.description: Leaked documents reveal that OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% in Q2 to -109% in Q3. Despite significant revenue growth, the company remains deep in the red due to massive compute costs, leaving profitability as a distant goal.

item.title: CoreWeave reports Q3 revenue up 168% YoY to $3.66B, vs. $3.55B est., a net loss of $709M, and a $132.5B revenue backlog, up from $104B as of June (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
item.description: CoreWeave reported a 168% YoY revenue increase to $3.66B in its latest quarterly report, and despite a $709M net loss, it raised its 2026 revenue guidance supported by a massive $132.5B backlog. This move aims to assure the market that demand for its GPU-rental services remains robust amid industry volatility.
